objectives: Recall the features and uses of computer interfaces and mobile computers
Identify benefits and limitations of desktops, laptops, smartphones and tablets
State effects of artificial intelligence on people and work
Give applications of extended reality and compare AR with VR
Answer eleven original Paper 1-style questions in about 35 minutes

practice.prompt: Tick (✓) whether each statement gives an advantage or a disadvantage of the named interface.

rows.statement: Spoken commands can help someone who finds physical controls difficult to use.
rows.explanation: A dialogue-based interface lets someone control equipment by speaking.

rows.statement: A dialogue-based interface may misunderstand instructions in a noisy place.
rows.explanation: Background sounds can make spoken instructions difficult to recognise.

rows.statement: Gesture controls can work without the person touching a switch.
rows.explanation: A sensor or camera can detect movements instead of requiring contact.

rows.statement: A gesture-controlled system may react to a movement the user did not intend as a command.
rows.explanation: Unwanted movements can be detected and trigger the wrong action.

practice.explanation: Two correctly classified statements earn one mark. Both interface types have useful features and possible problems.

practice.prompt: Match each situation in a school to the most suitable type of computer.

left.text: A fixed workstation with separate display and input equipment
A student carries a computer with a built-in physical keyboard
A learner taps an on-screen keyboard on a flat touch-screen device

practice.explanation: A desktop has separate parts, a laptop contains its keyboard and screen in one unit, and a tablet normally uses a touch-screen keyboard.

practice.prompt: State two advantages of using desktop computers instead of laptops in a permanent school computer room.

markPoints.point: Standardised spare parts / connections can make repairs less expensive
Easier / cheaper to upgrade or expand than laptops
Higher specification / faster processor for the same amount of money
Better heat removal from the larger case
More stable internet because desktop can use a wired connection
Less chance of theft / damage because the desktop stays in one place

practice.modelAnswer: Desktop components are usually easier to replace or upgrade. A desktop may also give a higher specification for the same price.
practice.explanation: State two different advantages. You do not have to explain them, but the points must favour the desktop rather than the laptop.

practice.prompt: Complete these statements about smartphone technology. Use each choice only once.

items.sentence: A phone may prevent unwanted screen taps near the user’s ear by using a ___.
A phone can detect a change in its orientation using an ___.
Files can be backed up and kept in sync online using ___.

practice.explanation: The proximity sensor detects nearby objects, the accelerometer detects movement or orientation, and cloud storage backs up or synchronises files.

practice.prompt: Give three disadvantages of using a smartphone rather than a laptop for schoolwork.

markPoints.point: Smaller display / reading long pages can be harder
Typing is slower / more difficult on a small on-screen keyboard
Battery can run down quickly when browsing / using the camera
Often has less storage / memory than a laptop
Some website functions may not work on the phone
Phone is easier to misplace / steal because it is small
Mobile network data may be slower than Wi-Fi for streaming

practice.modelAnswer: The small screen can make documents harder to read. Typing on a small keyboard can take longer. Using the internet and camera can drain the battery quickly.
practice.explanation: Give three distinct drawbacks. Repeating that the screen and keyboard are small in different words will not earn more than the separate screen and typing marks.

practice.prompt: State three advantages of tablets compared with laptops.

markPoints.point: Can start up / become ready to use quickly
reject: takes a long time to start

markPoints.point: Lightweight / easy to carry
Touch screen can be used without a separate pointing device / keyboard
Built-in programs / camera / media player are available
Produces little heat because of solid-state technology
Longer battery life than a laptop
Standby can stay online / receive alerts

practice.modelAnswer: A tablet is light enough to carry around. It can be controlled directly using a touch screen. It may last longer on its battery than a laptop.
practice.explanation: State three different advantages from the textbook. Each valid point earns one mark.

practice.prompt: (a) State what makes a phablet different in size from a smartphone and a tablet. [1] (b) Give two different everyday uses of mobile devices. [2]

markPoints.point: Phablet screen is larger than a smartphone screen but smaller than a tablet screen / about 5.1 to 7 inches in the textbook guide
accept: larger than a phone but smaller

markPoints.point: Using maps / GPS for navigation
Sending / receiving emails or instant messages
Online banking / transferring money
Education / interactive learning
Photography / recording videos
Watching / listening to online entertainment / playing games
Using internet apps to control home devices remotely

practice.modelAnswer: A phablet has a screen between the sizes of a smartphone and a tablet. Mobile devices can help people follow a map to a location. They can also control connected home equipment through an app.
practice.explanation: Part (a) earns one mark for the phablet size relationship. Part (b) earns one mark for each different everyday use.

practice.prompt: Give three possible effects of artificial intelligence on society. Include at least one benefit and one drawback.

markPoints.point: Benefit: machines may improve safety by carrying out risky work
Benefit: products / services may be improved in quality
Benefit: new technical jobs may be created
Drawback: workers may lose jobs / unemployment may rise
Drawback: people could become dependent on machines to complete tasks
Drawback: people may lose skills because they stop doing tasks themselves

practice.modelAnswer: Robots may make dangerous jobs safer for people. Some workers may lose jobs when machines take over tasks. People may also lose skills they no longer practise.
practice.explanation: Give three different effects. Since the question asks for both sides, include a benefit and a drawback.

practice.prompt: Give one application of augmented reality (AR) and one application of virtual reality (VR). Label each example.

markPoints.point: AR: show a rescue team a 3D model to help plan procedures
AR: preview make-up on a real face before purchase
AR: create a 3D view of a patient using scans
VR: train staff / practise a medical or military procedure in a simulated environment
VR: explore a historic place or ancient building in a virtual environment
VR: examine a digital scientific model of a cell or molecule
VR: practise sport with feedback / experience a game

practice.modelAnswer: AR can be used to preview a digital make-up design on a real face. VR can be used to explore a simulated historic building in a lesson.
practice.explanation: Award one mark for an AR example and one for a VR example. Put each use under the correct label.

practice.prompt: A teacher is visiting a nature reserve where there is no Wi-Fi, but a mobile phone network is available. Explain how a smartphone could help her send photographs to students at school.

markPoints.point: Smartphone has a camera / can capture pictures of the reserve
Smartphone can connect to the internet through a mobile phone network without Wi-Fi
Teacher can email / share the pictures with students while away from school

practice.modelAnswer: The smartphone has a camera for taking photographs at the nature reserve. It can connect to the internet through the available mobile phone network. The teacher can send the pictures to her students while she is away from school.
practice.explanation: Link the phone features to the trip. A camera captures the images, and mobile internet allows sharing without Wi-Fi.

practice.prompt: Compare augmented reality with virtual reality. Give three differences. In each difference, describe both technologies.

markPoints.point: AR adds digital information to a real scene, whereas VR shows a completely simulated scene
accept: ar adds to real while vr replaces
ar over real whereas vr virtual
ar adds objects but vr simulates
ar real view while vr fully digital

markPoints.point: AR can use a smartphone / phablet screen or special goggles, whereas VR uses a head-mounted display or headset
accept: ar can use screen but vr headset
reject: vr does not use a headset
ar only works with vr headset

markPoints.point: AR user still sees / interacts with real surroundings, whereas VR user is immersed and visually separated from the real surroundings
accept: ar sees room whereas vr hidden
ar can see real but vr not
ar real surroundings while vr immersed
ar interacts real while vr virtual
reject: vr same real view as ar

practice.modelAnswer: AR adds digital content to the real environment, whereas VR replaces the scene with a simulated one. AR can be viewed through a phone or special goggles, whereas VR uses a head-mounted display. An AR user can still interact with physical surroundings, whereas a VR user is immersed in a virtual world.
practice.explanation: A difference needs both sides of the comparison. Three separate contrasts earn three marks. Do not just describe AR without describing VR.

summary: Dialogue-based interfaces accept speech; gesture-based interfaces detect movements using a sensor or camera.
Desktops use separate components. Laptops are portable single units with built-in keyboards.
Smartphones use apps, cameras and sensors; tablets favour touch input; phablets sit between phones and tablets in the textbook size guide.
AI can make some tasks safer and improve quality, but may also cause job losses, dependence and reduced human skills.
AR adds digital content to a real view, while VR provides a simulated environment through a headset.

flashcards.front: What is the main difference between dialogue and gesture interfaces?
flashcards.back: Dialogue uses spoken instructions; gesture control uses movements detected by cameras or sensors.

flashcards.front: Why can a desktop be easier to upgrade than a laptop?
flashcards.back: Desktop parts are usually more standard and easier to replace or add.

flashcards.front: What do a proximity sensor and an accelerometer detect?
flashcards.back: A proximity sensor detects nearby objects; an accelerometer detects movement and orientation.
A mobile device with a screen between smartphone and tablet sizes in the textbook guide.

flashcards.front: Name one benefit and one drawback of AI.
flashcards.back: A benefit is safer dangerous work. A drawback is possible job losses.

flashcards.front: How do AR and VR differ?
flashcards.back: AR overlays digital content on the physical world. VR shows a simulated world, usually through a headset.
